theoremName: continuous residual-to-solution inclusion for the undivided endpoint graph DAE
statement: Let qhat be a C1 approximate solution of the undivided graph DAE. On regular intervals the stated Gronwall radius encloses an exact solution. Across a simple zero a=(s-s*)alpha with p=c/alpha>=p0>0, every positive root interval of the stated singular radii polynomial contains a unique bounded exact graph solution.

domain.unknown: q in C^1(J; R^7) on regular pieces and q continuous/bounded with x q' continuous at the crossing
domain.coefficientSpace: a,c,d continuous; alpha,p continuous at the simple crossing; B fixed
domain.norm: componentwise vector sup norm and induced matrix infinity norm
domain.crossingSelection: the unique bounded solution germ; evaluating the exact equation at x=0 gives c(s*)q(s*)+d(s*)=0

equation: a(q' + q B + (q b) q) + c q + d = 0

regularEstimate.conclusion: an exact solution with the same incoming datum lies in the rho sup ball about qhat

hypotheses: p >= p0 > 0 on both half intervals
crossingEstimate.conclusion: a unique bounded exact solution lies in the rho sup ball about qhat on |s-s*|<=h

proof.regular: Subtract the exact and approximate equations, divide only where |a|>=a0, bound the graph nonlinearity by (||B||+2||b||(Q+rho))||w||, and apply the variation-of-constants formula and Gronwall's inequality.
proof.crossing: After a=x alpha, the error equation is (x d/dx+p)w=-r/alpha-x[N(qhat+w)-N(qhat)]. On either half interval the integrating factor mu(x)=exp(int p(t)dt/t) gives ||(x d/dx+p)^(-1)||<=1/p0 on bounded functions. The displayed radii and derivative inequalities make the fixed-point map invariant and contractive. The complementary homogeneous solution is mu^(-1) and is unbounded, so boundedness supplies uniqueness and transmission through x=0. The common limiting value automatically satisfies the exact algebraic equation at the crossing; the approximate graph need not satisfy it exactly because its mismatch is part of r.
